results.reason: The abstract describes a search-based technique for unit test generation on object-oriented programs that reaches higher coverage than random testing, which matches the claim.
The abstract reports that test suites detecting more mutants also detect more real faults, so mutation scores are a useful proxy, matching the citing sentence.
The abstract finds that 14 percent of CI test failures were caused by flaky tests, which supports the claim that flaky tests are common in continuous integration.

The abstract describes a genetic-algorithm-based search for unit tests, which matches the attribution of a GA-style approach to this work. The mutant-specific search is not described, but the cited attribution concerns the GA style.
The abstract describes a fuzzer that uses coverage feedback to find crashes, consistent with the claim about coverage-guided input mutation in fuzzing.

The abstract says the search is guided by a genetic algorithm maximizing branch coverage, consistent with optimizing coverage. It does not mention mutants, which is consistent with the claim that it does not use them.
The abstract studies whether mutants are a valid substitute for real faults and finds mutation scores useful, which supports motivating the use of mutants.
The abstract measures how common flaky tests are (14 percent of CI failures), which matches the attribution of measuring frequency.
The abstract describes a coverage-guided fuzzer that finds crashes in parsers, consistent with fuzzers sharing input mutation and targeting crashes.
